newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Gold - Price under threat of further fall.
newsitem.headline: Australia Gold - Price under threat of further fall.

text.p: Gold is under threat of losing more ground in international markets after failing to stage much of a recovery this week.
Bullion dealers in Australia said technical support points could come under pressure in European and U.S. trading later on Thursday as gold's gliter continues to fade among investors.

The weakness in the gold price, which left bullion 70 cents lower at US$317.80/30 in New York overnight is seen as helping vindicate recent decisions by some of Australia's mining houses to postpone expansion plans.
The most dramatic decision has come from WMC Ltd, which has put a A$157 million expansion of its St Ives mine in Western Australia on hold, owing to a poor outlook for gold prices.
The expansion would have eventually lifted the yield at St Ives to around 700,000 ounces a year from 400,000 ounces.

WMC managing director Hugh Morgan also faces criticism for allowing himself as a Board member of Australia's Reserve Bank to be part of the decision by the RBA to sell two-thirds of its gold reserves.
Morgan has denied any wrongdoing, saying he never used his position at the bank to benefit WMC.
Morgan's statement followed Australian media comments that WMC's gold hedging programme had thrown into question the role of independent board members of the Reserve Bank.
WMC's gold hedge book rose to 3.04 million ounces as at June 30 from 727,000 ounces at the end of September 1996.

On a smaller scale, General Gold NL is shutting down its Mount Monger mine in Western Australia and North Ltd has cast doubt over the near-term development its Lake Cowal gold mine in New South Wales.
But the greatest impact may be a growing inability to raise capital for further exploration and project development.

"The falling gold price will make underwriters extremely nervous and will affect the ability of explorers to raise further funds for exploration and development," said Greg Wheeler, a partner in the Grant Thornton accounting firm.
"We already have the situation in Australia where brokers are too risk averse and overly conservative," he said. This will only add their nervousness."

Concerns over the possibility of a a free-for-all of undisciplined sales by central banks is undermining the chances of a recovery in the gold price, North deputy managing director Malcom Broomhead said.
Broomhead agrees with others in the industry that the current market leaves more Australian gold miners exposed to takeovers since many mines carry cash costs below the spot price.
Speculation persists that Great Central Mines Ltd may be targeted for takeover by Canada's Barrick Gold Corp.

Great Central is viewed as an attractive target for a North American gold company because it has reserves of more than a million ounces of gold, in excess of 500,000 ounces a year of low-cost gold production and upside for reserves and output.
